authoring_notes.structure: 22 chapters across 7 phases. Reduced from a 30-chapter draft per learner request. Theory-first: ch-01..ch-04 are math foundations + numerical formats; no LLM-specific algorithm appears in deps until ch-05. The 2022 -> 2026 LLM quantization literature is sequenced chronologically across phases 3-6. Eval methodology (ch-20), lab (ch-21), capstone (ch-22) close the course.
authoring_notes.reduction_rationale: Original 30-chapter draft had several closely-related chapters that read as one topic in practice. Mergers applied: (1) Lloyd-Max + calibration objectives -> ch-03; (2) STE chapter + QAT survivors + AdaRound/BRECQ -> ch-04; (3) PTQ playbook + Hessian lineage -> ch-05; (4) GPTQ + ZeroQuant -> ch-08; (5) 2024 rotations + AQLM + HQQ -> ch-14 (single W4A4 + sub-2-bit chapter); (6) BitNet origins + b1.58 + a4.8 + microscaling formats -> ch-16; (7) FP8 native training + NVFP4/MXFP4 + Blackwell -> ch-17 (single low-precision-pretraining chapter); (8) data-oblivious KV trio + 2026 KV frontier -> ch-18.
authoring_notes.theory_first_rule: Per CLAUDE.md, the first 4 chapters MUST source only from `classics/` and `formats/` in the raw library. LLM papers (GPTQ, AWQ, SmoothQuant, etc.) do not appear in deps until ch-05.
authoring_notes.year_progression: Phase 3 = 2022 (LLM PTQ born). Phase 4 = 2023 (explosion). Phase 5 = 2024 (rotations, KV-cache, BitNet b1.58, microscaling). Phase 6 = 2025-2026 (FP8/FP4 native training, data-oblivious KV, production kernels).
authoring_notes.per_chapter_format: Each ch-XX/read.md (~200-250 lines) quotes the actual quantization rule / Hessian update / bit layout / kernel pseudocode from the raw-data source. ch-XX/excerpts/ contains 3-5 per-source extract files (~50-80 lines each) with verbatim equations + key quotes from the cited papers. ch-XX/figures/ is OPTIONAL: include only when a parameter explorer / bit-layout diagram / rate-distortion curve / outlier-distribution viz adds real understanding.
authoring_notes.depth_target: Math chapters (ch-01..ch-04) MUST include explicit equations and worked derivations. Algorithm chapters MUST include the verbatim quantization rule, the exact group/block size, the calibration objective, and at least one concrete model x bit-width perplexity/accuracy number from the source paper.
authoring_notes.outdated_knowledge_policy: For 2026 frontier chapters (ch-17..ch-20), claims should be anchored to the raw-data source's snapshot. When the source says 'as of Nov 2025' or similar, preserve that framing rather than asserting current truth.
authoring_notes.intended_format: Self-study program for a learner targeting production + research depth on LLM quantization. The first 6 chapters provide a one-week math/format foundation; the 2022-2026 algorithm chain runs 12 chapters; the lab + capstone close.
authoring_notes.lab_paths: Lab (ch-21) and capstone (ch-22) each offer two execution paths: full-budget (H100 + Llama-3-8B end-to-end) and resource-constrained (single consumer GPU + 1B-3B model). Memo / artifact requirement is the same in both paths -- only training scale differs.

tracks.title: Classical PTQ and the Bridge to LLMs
2025-2026 Frontier: Low-Precision Pretraining + Data-Oblivious KV + Production

chapters.title: Rate-Distortion + Math Foundations of Quantization
concepts: Shannon rate-distortion R(D); Gaussian closed form D = sigma^2 * 2^(-2R); the floor every quantizer fights
Bennett uniform-noise model: sigma_q^2 = Delta^2 / 12; high-resolution assumption + when it breaks
Gish-Pierce optimal density rho(x) proportional to p(x)^(1/3); why non-uniform spacing wins for LLM weights
Stochastic rounding vs round-to-nearest-even; preserving unbiasedness at low precision
Mapping these bounds onto observed LLM weight + activation distributions

chapters.title: Numerical Formats Reference: FP / INT / Block-Scaled
concepts: IEEE-754 binary32/binary16 reference; exponent vs mantissa; subnormals; rounding modes
BF16 vs FP16 trade-off (same exponent as FP32 vs half the dynamic range); why BF16 dominated training
FP8 family: E4M3 (forward) vs E5M2 (backward); FP6 / FP4 (E2M1) progression
INT8 / INT4 with symmetric vs asymmetric scale; per-tensor / per-channel / per-group granularity
Block-scaled formats: OCP MX (32-element block + E8M0 shared exponent), NVFP4 (16-element block + E4M3 fractional scale + FP32 tensor scale), NF4 (quantile-based code), BitNet w1.58 (ternary)

chapters.title: Quantizer Design: Uniform vs Non-Uniform + Calibration Objectives
concepts: Lloyd-Max iteration: centroid + nearest-neighbour conditions; convergence
K-means as scalar VQ; LBG algorithm; product quantization (PQ) groups dimensions and stores K-means codes
Companding (mu-law / A-law): the original 'log-scale' non-uniform quantizer; analog to NF4
Calibration objectives: MSE vs KL vs Hessian-weighted; when each one matters
Percentile clipping vs full-range vs MSE-optimal clip; outlier handling at calibration time

chapters.title: STE + QAT Lineage: BNN -> LSQ -> AdaRound
concepts: STE forward: q(x) = round(x/Delta)*Delta; backward: identity gradient; why this biased gradient still works
BNN / XNOR-Net: original 1-bit weight + activation; binary conv via XNOR + popcount
DoReFa / PACT: arbitrary-bit quantizer family + learned activation clipping threshold
LSQ (learned step size): scale s as a learnable parameter; gradient = -floor(x/s) + clamp(x/s); SOTA QAT baseline
AdaRound: per-weight learned rounding direction via rectified sigmoid; closed-form Hessian objective; the spiritual parent of GPTQ

chapters.title: Classical PTQ Playbook + OBS -> GPTQ Lineage
concepts: Krishnamoorthi 2018 taxonomy: PTQ vs QAT; symmetric vs asymmetric; per-tensor vs per-channel; min-max vs MSE calibration
Data-free quantization (DFQ): weight equalization + bias correction without calibration data
BRECQ: block-wise reconstruction objective; why per-block beats per-layer at low-bit PTQ
Optimal Brain Surgeon (Hassibi 1993): second-order weight removal with inverse-Hessian update
Optimal Brain Compression (Frantar 2022): unified pruning + quantization via shared OBS objective; the direct parent of GPTQ

chapters.title: Integer-Only Inference: Jacob 2018 + I-BERT
concepts: Jacob 2018 INT8-only inference: requant pipeline M = S_w*S_x/S_y approximated as M_0 * 2^(-n); INT8 GEMM on ARM
I-BERT integer-only approximations: i-GELU polynomial, integer Softmax, integer LayerNorm
Q-BERT mixed-precision Hessian-aware quant for BERT; precursor to LLM mixed-precision
ZeroQ data-free calibration via BN statistics; the bridge from CNN PTQ to transformer PTQ
What integer-only gives you (zero FP fallback, mobile-CPU-only inference) and what it costs (more engineering for non-linearities)

chapters.title: LLM.int8() and the Outlier Discovery
concepts: Emergent outlier features at 6.7B+: empirical discovery + theoretical interpretation
Mixed-precision decomposition: per-row INT8 GEMM + FP16 outlier columns (|x| > 6.0 threshold)
Vector-wise scale: per-token activation scale + per-channel weight scale
Practical recipe: bitsandbytes 'load_in_8bit' under the hood
What LLM.int8 left unsolved: weight-only PTQ at <= 4 bits, activation quant below 8 bits

chapters.title: GPTQ at Scale + ZeroQuant Family
concepts: GPTQ Cholesky block update: process columns in blocks, update remaining via inverse-Hessian Cholesky factor
act_order trick: descending diag(H) ordering recovers ~0.1-0.3 PPL at 4-bit
percdamp + group_size: numerical stability damping + per-group scale; the standard W4A16 recipe
ZeroQuant: INT8 group-wise weight + token-wise activation + layer-wise KD recovery; ZeroQuant-V2 low-rank residual; ZeroQuant-FP shows FP4/FP8 can beat INT at low bits
From algorithm to kernel: Marlin's W4A16 GEMM as the production realisation of GPTQ

chapters.title: SmoothQuant + AWQ -- Activation-Aware Equivalent Transformations
concepts: Activation-outlier problem: activations have channels 10-100x larger than typical; weights are well-behaved
SmoothQuant equivalent transformation: diag(s) * X with s_j = max(|X_j|)^alpha / max(|W_j|)^(1-alpha); migration parameter alpha
AWQ: per-channel scaling s_j driven by activation magnitude; grid-search over alpha; no backprop; the W4A16 default
Salient channels: empirical finding that ~1 % of weight columns dominate output error
Production: AWQ + Marlin/Machete is the canonical W4A16 deployment stack

chapters.title: OmniQuant + Learnable Equivalent Transformations
concepts: Learnable Weight Clipping (LWC): per-channel learned clipping bounds trained via block-wise MSE
Learnable Equivalent Transformation (LET): make AWQ's per-channel scale learnable
Block-wise gradient-based PTQ: differentiate through STE, optimize the transformations, no full backprop through the whole model
AffineQuant and FlatQuant: affine transformations that flatten the activation distribution
RPTQ: reorder channels into similar-range clusters as a complementary trick

chapters.title: SqueezeLLM + SpQR -- Sensitivity-Aware + Sparse-and-Dense
concepts: Sensitivity-weighted k-means: cluster weights by Fisher-information importance; non-uniform code per channel
Dense-and-sparse decomposition: top 0.5 % outlier weights stay in FP16, rest quantized aggressively
SpQR bilevel grouping: FP16 outlier matrix as compact sparse format alongside group-wise quant
OWQ outlier-aware weight quantization: lighter-weight sparse-and-dense variant
The lesson: outliers are signal, not noise; preserve them precisely

chapters.title: QLoRA + NF4 -- 4-bit Fine-Tuning at Consumer Scale
concepts: NF4 (Normal Float 4-bit): quantile-based 16-level code for the Gaussian weight prior
Double quantization: quantize per-block scales themselves to FP8; saves ~ 0.5 bit/element
Paged optimizer: NVIDIA UVM for optimizer states; fine-tune 65B on a single 48 GB GPU
LoRA adapters in BF16 on top of the 4-bit frozen base; what is actually trained
QA-LoRA / LoftQ / LLM-QAT: alternatives that push the quant-aware-finetune frontier

chapters.title: QuIP + Incoherence Processing (Rotation Preview)
concepts: Incoherence processing: random orthogonal U, V applied to W to spread the energy
LDLQ adaptive rounding: the optimal-rounding step QuIP runs after rotation
QuIP# E8 lattice codebook: 2-bit code per group with high packing efficiency
Randomized Hadamard transform: the practical realisation of the random orthogonal (O(d log d), structure-preserving)
Bridge: rotation idea is the seed that explodes into QuaRot / SpinQuant / DuQuant in 2024

chapters.title: 2024 W4A4 + Sub-2-bit: Rotations + AQLM + HQQ
concepts: QuaRot: random Hadamard rotations folded into weights for W4A4 PTQ; orthogonal property preserves outputs
SpinQuant: learnable orthogonal rotations via Cayley-parametrized SGD on the Stiefel manifold
DuQuant: dual block-rotation + channel-permutation for outlier removal
AQLM additive quantization: w approx sum_m C_m[i_m]; M codebooks of K vectors; PQ-inspired sub-2-bit; PV-Tuning fine-tunes the discrete indices
HQQ Half-Quadratic Quantization: alternating closed-form steps; data-free, very fast; the 'iterate quickly' tool
Production: QServe (W4A8KV4) and Atom (W4A4KV4) show what these methods look like under a serving stack

chapters.title: KV-Cache Quantization: KIVI / KVQuant / GEAR
concepts: Why KV-cache memory dominates long-context inference; bandwidth-bound decode
K vs V asymmetry: K has channel-aligned outliers (RoPE-induced); V is roughly Gaussian per token
KIVI: per-channel K + per-token V; INT2 viable; the canonical recipe
KVQuant: dense-and-sparse for K cache + non-uniform per-channel quant; sub-2-bit V
GEAR error compensation + WKVQuant joint calibration + SKVQ sliding-window; the design space of KV PTQ

chapters.title: BitNet Lineage + Microscaling Formats
concepts: BitLinear layer: sign quantization with absmean scale; STE backward; replaces nn.Linear
BitNet b1.58: ternary {-1, 0, +1} per-tensor absmean rounding; log2(3) ~ 1.58 bits/weight; FP16 perplexity parity claimed at >= 3B scale
BitNet a4.8: 4-bit activations on top of 1.58-bit weights; absmean activation scaling
OneBit SVID decomposition: 1-bit weight via sign matrix + scaling vectors
Microscaling formats (OCP MX, 2023): shared 8-bit exponent block + low-bit element; the cross-vendor standard that NVFP4 sits alongside

chapters.title: Low-Precision Pretraining: FP8 DeepSeek V3 + NVFP4/MXFP4 + Blackwell
concepts: DeepSeek V3 FP8 native training: per-block scaling (1x128 activation tiles, 128x128 weight blocks); BF16 master weights; FP32 accumulation every 4 WGMMA
Transformer Engine FP8 recipe: per-tensor delayed scaling, amax history, E4M3 forward + E5M2 backward split
NVFP4 native pretraining (Blackwell): two-level scaling FP8 block-scale + FP32 tensor-scale; FP4 forward + FP8 backward
MXFP4 pretraining diagnostics: stochastic rounding requirement, gradient clipping at higher precision, native-hardware-vs-emulated gap
Why FP8 -> FP4 in training: 2-4x throughput on Blackwell; <= 1% downstream quality cost with quant-aware distillation (NVFP4-QAD)

chapters.title: Data-Oblivious KV + 2026 KV Frontier
concepts: QJL: 1-bit Johnson-Lindenstrauss sketch with asymmetric inner-product estimator; zero per-block metadata overhead
PolarQuant: recursive pair-wise polar transform after random preconditioning; closed-form angle distribution; > 4.2x KV compression
TurboQuant: random rotation + per-coordinate scalar quant + 1-bit QJL residual; matches rate-distortion bound up to constant; 2.5-3.5 bit KV with no calibration
The data-oblivious thesis: eliminate calibration via high-dimensional measure concentration after rotation
KVTC and adaptive KV-cache precision: 2026 extensions that combine quant with per-token bit allocation

chapters.title: Production Quant Kernels + Deployment Stacks
concepts: Marlin W4A16 GEMM: async copies + warp-specialized dequant pipeline + double-buffered shared memory; near-FP16 throughput at low batch
Machete (Hopper TMA + WGMMA): vLLM-native W4A16; benchmark vs Marlin
TensorRT-LLM quant path: GPTQ/AWQ/FP8/SmoothQuant/NVFP4 integration; calibration -> engine build
vLLM QuantConfig: how AutoGPTQ / AutoAWQ models load; Marlin / Machete as runtime kernels
llama.cpp gguf k-quant ladder: q2_K through q8_0; super-block structure; community curators (bartowski)

chapters.title: Quantization Evaluation Methodology
concepts: When perplexity lies: PPL is sensitive to layer-norm gain scales; small PPL changes can correspond to large MMLU shifts
Statistically-lossless quantization: defining 'no quality loss' rigorously via confidence intervals over a benchmark suite
Per-layer sensitivity diagnostics: FP4-inference-diagnosis-style approach to finding which layers tolerate which bit-widths
Long-context-specific evaluation: NIAH, RULER, LongBench under quant; KV-quant changes the failure modes
Calibration set design: size, source, distribution shift; why 128 sequences usually suffices for GPTQ but not for activation-aware methods

chapters.title: Lab -- Quantize an Open Model End-to-End
concepts: Full-budget path: Llama-3-8B + H100; AutoGPTQ-W4 + AutoAWQ-W4 + QLoRA-NF4 + bitsandbytes-INT8; perplexity + 5 task evals
Resource-constrained path: Qwen-1.8B + single 16 GB GPU; same quant methods at smaller scale; subset of evals
Memo deliverable: side-by-side table of perplexity / accuracy / latency / memory across the 4 quant methods + FP16 baseline
Required ablation: change group_size, alpha (AWQ), or LoRA rank and report the effect
Reflection: which method is on the Pareto frontier for which workload (latency-bound vs memory-bound vs fine-tune-required)

chapters.title: Capstone -- Reproduce a Frontier Method on a Small LLM
concepts: Pick one of {KIVI, KVQuant, GEAR, TurboQuant, NVFP4 inference}; implement from the paper (no copy-paste from author repo)
Full-budget path: H100 + Llama-3-8B; long-context eval (LongBench, NIAH, RULER); 3-bit and 2-bit KV target
Resource-constrained path: single 24 GB GPU + TinyLlama-1.1B-chat; reduced context length but full method
Reproduction memo: did you match the paper's reported numbers within 2 %? If not, where is the gap and why
Optional stretch: combine KV-quant with W4A4 weight quant (QuaRot + KV method) and report the multiplicative compounding effect
